item.title: Riley Sheehan hits out at selectors after missing USA Road Worlds selection
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Sheehan didn't make the eight-man team for the 273km elite men's race. Instead, selectors picked Matteo Jorgenson, Brandon McNulty, Neilson Powless, Sean Quinn, Artem Shmidt, Quinn Simmons, Kevin Vermaerke, and Larry Warbasse."Let's not select the guys who've been winning races…" Sheehan wrote in a post on Twitter.Former Paris-Tours champion Sheehan, 26, has taken two wins this season, triumphing at the Circuit de Wallonie and stage 1 of the recent Czech Tour. He also finished runner-up at June's Tour de Wallonie.Of the eight riders selected, five of them have yet to win a race in 2026, including Jorgenson and McNulty.Powless, Shmidt, and Simmons have taken five wins between them this season, including US road and time trial titles, the Classique Dunkerque, and stages of the Tour of Austria and the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes.Sheehan has raced the elite Road Worlds once before, registering a DNF in Zurich, Switzerland, two years ago.He has been one of the USA's top-performing racers this year, currently the nation's sixth-highest rider in the UCI rankings on 695 points.Above him, Matthew Riccitello and Sepp Kuss were also not selected, though both are in the midst of racing the Tour-Vuelta double.USA Cycling's selection policy emphasises past Worlds results before looking at rider's stand-out results in a range of other races throughout the calendar."Any athlete who earns a top five (5) in a European UCI World Tour one-day race (1.WWT, 1.UWT) on a course similar in length, profile and demands as the 2026 World Championships Road Race between the dates of January 1, 2026, and August 16, 2026, will be nominated to the Team," the policy reads."If quota positions remain after considering the preceding criteria, any athlete who earns a top five (5) General Classification in a European UCI World Tour stage race (2.WWT, 2.UWT) between the dates of January 1, 2026, and August 16, 2026, will be nominated to the Team."If quota positions remain after considering the preceding criteria, the winner of the 2026 USA Cycling Elite Road Race National Championships, provided the race is held in its entirety and run under UCI regulations, will be nominated to the Team. "If quota positions remain after considering the preceding criteria, athletes may be nominated to the Team through discretionary criteria."The USA men's team will head to Canada looking to improve on recent results at the Road Worlds, with standouts over the past three years being 11th by Powless in 2023 and ninth by Simmons in 2024.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: US racer Ezra Caudell remains in hospital with 'multi-system trauma' after Philadelphia Cycling Classic crash
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Caudell was involved in a crash early in Sunday's race, colliding with Lotto-Intermarché rider Milan Menten. He was knocked unconscious in the accident, according to a report by .The 19-year-old's team have now given details on his condition in a statement released on Tuesday night."Ezra remains hospitalized and is actively receiving care for multi-system trauma he sustained as a result of his crash at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic," the statement read."He has an incredible team working diligently and family at his bedside. We are grateful for the thoughts and ongoing outpouring of support."On Monday, Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker thanked first responders at the scene, noting that both Caudell and Menten were taken to hospitals after the crash."We are also closely monitoring two cyclists from the men’s race who were injured and required treatment at local hospitals," she said, according to ."City first responders, including our Fire Department, on-site medical personnel, and my leadership team responded immediately to the incident, and I am grateful for their service. My team and I are at the hospital now."Lotto-Intermarché have yet to release a statement on Milan Menten's condition.Caudell, who turns 20 on September 8, scored top 10s in three USPro Road Championships races in June, including fourth in the U23 road race and one day later went seventh in the elite men's road race. His teammate Ben Oliver finished seventh on Sunday in the Philadelphia race.Tim Torn Teutenberg (Lidl-Trek) eventually won the men's race in a three-man sprint against Robert Donaldson (Jayco-AlUla) and Jonas Rutsch (Lotto-Intermarché), while Chiara Consonni (Canyon-SRAM) beat Alexandra Volstad (EF Education-Oatly) to the line in a seven-rider sprint to win the women's race.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Automatic suspension, string spokes, and custom brakes: Evie Richards' unreleased Trek flex-stay prototype from Val di Sole
item.content:encoded: Silver by a tyre's width. That's how Evie Richards' 2026 short track world championship ended in Val di Sole; out-sprinted on the line by Austria's Laura Stigger after a race that had both the Italian crowds and me on our feet for all ten laps. It's the sort of result that could read as heartbreak or as vindication, depending on the season you've had. For Richards, though, it's probably a bit of both.Richards arrived in Val di Sole with a palmarès few in the field can match: elite cross-country world champion in 2021, Commonwealth Games gold in 2022, two under-23 cyclo-cross world titles either side of that, and, more recently, the overall World Series short-track crown in 2025. She's a rider whose punchy full-gas style is built for exactly this kind of race: short, sharp, tactical, and flat out from the start.What makes it remarkable is how she managed to be at the sharp end at all, given the challenging season she's had.2026 has been brutal for Richards, even by mountain biking's unforgiving standards. She opened the World Cup campaign in YongPyong carrying the aftermath of injury and still managed second in the short track opener, then came Nové Město: fourth in the XCC, before a horror crash in the following XCO race sent her over the bars at speed on a technical section. X-rays cleared her neck, but the head impact was serious enough to floor her for weeks, layering yet another concussion onto a rap sheet that already includes a partially dislocated knee, a lower back injury and a string of wrist problems. XC MTB takes no prisoners, and can be a real test of a rider's character.Racing again by La Thuile was impressive enough, but ending up on a world championship podium in Val di Sole a matter of weeks later is truly remarkable.The Bike: Trek's still-unnamed flex-stay prototypeThe machine underneath her for that short track final is the same one that turned heads when it broke cover earlier in the season: an unreleased, unnamed Trek prototype that the brand itself said: "may never hit store shelves." It replaces the modified Top Fuel downcountry platform Richards raced last year, a bike that always looked slightly overbuilt for XC racing and felt more like a trail bike.The new frame runs a flex-stay rear end, ditching a pivot at the dropouts to save weight and bearings while keeping the suspension responsive enough for Val di Sole's brutal descents. The XCC course is smoother and less technical, so some changes come from tyre pressure and inserts, but settings remain very similar across both disciplines.Speaking of bars, she runs a one-piece bar and stem from Trek's in-house brand Bontrager and goes for a 760mm width. Some riders run narrower bars for Short Course, but not here. They are also custom-painted purple to match the rest of the bike.

item.title: Picnic-PostNL lose key director Matt Winston as well as two other coaches
item.content:encoded: On top of the rider transfer market, there have been plenty of moves in the managerial market, and the latest sees Picnic-PostNL lose one of their leading sports directors in Matt Winston, as well as two other coaches.The Briton, who previously worked at the British Cycling federation, joined the Dutch team under the title of Race Coach in 2019, and went on to establish himself as a key figure in the team car at the Tour de France and other major races. "The team will say goodbye to coach Matt Winston at the end of the 2026 season, as he leaves the team to take on a new challenge elsewhere," read a statement from Picnic-PostNL."After eight years together, the team look back on a strong and valued collaboration and thank Matt for his commitment and contribution to the team throughout this period and wish him every success in his next chapter."Picnic-PostNL are also losing two other coaches in Davide Gani and Melvin Rulliere, in what must be considered a new blow in the midst of an utterly miserable season in terms of results. The team have announced an 'evolution' of its coaching structure, with Roy Curvers promoted to a senior position as part of what it terms the Sportive Management of the team.The Dutchman is a stalwart of the team, riding for them for 12 seasons before slotting straight into a coaching role in 2020, first in the Development squad and then with the WorldTour team. "During that time, he has developed within our organisation not only as a coach, but also by broadening his management and leadership skills and taking on increasing responsibility within the team."His extensive experience, natural leadership and deep understanding of the team, the culture and the way of working make him the right person to help lead the next phase of our sporting structure. In his new role, Roy will join Rudi Kemna, as part of sportive management."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: This data has helped fight workplace discrimination for 60 years. The Trump administration plans to delete it
item.author: Amy Qin
item.content:encoded: Enforcing civil rights without these reports will be difficult for the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, pushing US agency closer to Trump’s agenda, experts warnThe US civil rights agency mandated to protect equal rights for workers is set to stop collecting data on the demographic makeup of companies – which for the past six decades has been used to enforce anti-discrimination laws.The move marks a fundamental shift for the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). Without this data, it will be much harder for the agency to identify widespread cases of discrimination in hiring and promotions, experts and former employees of the commission say. And, they warn, it will bring the Trump administration one step closer to reshaping the commission from an independent watchdog into an arm of the executive branch narrowly focused on advancing the political grievances of Donald Trump’s base.Continue reading...

item.title: Knicks Bulletin: ‘We don’t talk about the trophy’
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: We’re already into September, and that can only mean one thing: we’re back in business.Starting today, your freshest and first Bulletin of the 2027-28 NBA season.(Here’s a small bunch of quotes, because the calendar page might have flipped but it’s not that we’re already close to anything of importance.) On putting last season’s championship behind entering their title defense:“We don’t want to speak of the trophy, we don’t talk about the trophy, we don’t want to see the trophy. We want to come in with the same mindset, if not, even a tougher mindset than we had last year… It’s important for us to come into this season to be like, ‘That’s over with.’”On modeling his early career stint in Dallas after JJ Barea:“My mindset was, I’m filling JJ Barea’s role. He came off the bench for Dallas. He did all these great things for Dallas. That’s where I see myself. I’m gonna work to be better, but that’s where I see myself. That’s where I feel like I can help this team.“The more you show in your role, the longer your leash gets, the more you’re able to do. People just want to say, ‘Hey, I can do this, I can do that.’ Well, do what’s asked of you first. Perfect it. Master it.”On refusing to call himself the “King of New York”:“I’ve never called myself the king of New York. I will never call myself the king of New York.“Imagine I get on this call with you, right? I’m like, ‘Yo, no king of New York’s here,’ whatever, whatever. You guys are going to look like, ‘What the f**k, this dude is so self-centered.’”On staying grounded as his profile has grown:“I just find a way to kind of be the same because of the people around me. I have the same people I had around since high school.”On the belief that powered the Knicks’ championship run:“Believe. That’s one thing you got to do is believe. The way we did it, 53 years, a lot of people say we were supposed to be there but still doubted us. A lot of people thought the first round was a way out because how we started. So I guess faith, believe. We just believed in each other, we believed in what we could do and that’s what made us champions.”On his goal of becoming a Sixth Man of the Year candidate:“I still haven’t done what I wanted to do with my career. I got a lot of goals that I want to push for and this is probably going to be the most hard-working summer I probably put in. I want to be in the conversation of Sixth Man of the Year one day. Obviously I got to work, obviously situations where the minutes, consistency and stuff like that is always going to be a problem because I know I’m never going to pass the eye test. If you look at me, I’m not the most tallest, most athletic to the NBA world. So I just know going into a room, I got to be the most out-working person, hardest-working person and the rest will take care of itself.”On representing the Philippines:“When you got Filipino blood, [you] take the whole country with you, the whole pride.“We’re doing a lot for the country and the culture.”On Jalen Brunson being New York’s king:“I’m happy as the mayor. Jalen Brunson is the king.”On wanting to become Team USA’s general manager:“One of my main goals is to be the GM of Team USA. In one of these Olympics, one of these years, I want to do that job one time.”On the globalization of basketball and international players becoming the NBA’s best:“Our game is global. We play basketball all around the world (…) And it’s about time. They’ve been coming into the league since the 80s. It’s just natural evolution that guys from around the world are going to assume those positions as the best players in the league.”

item.title: After MTB world title, Tom Pidcock turns focus to UCI Road World Championships with build-up in Canada
item.content:encoded: There had been reports in various media outlets that Pidcock was down to ride the Tour of Britain starting on Wednesday, but his Pinarello-Q36.5 team confirmed to that it was never part of any plans to participate in his home race. Instead, Pidcock will soon travel to Canada, where he will line up at both of the two WorldTour one-day races, the Grand Prix de Québec on Friday, September 11 and the Grand Prix de Montréal on Sunday, September 13. The two races are always big events, but this year they are an obvious stepping stone towards the Road World Championships, with the elite men's road race taking place in Montreal on September 27.Pidcock has not raced on the road since placing 9th overall at the Tour de France, a creditable result but one that didn't yield a stage win or build on his breakout Vuelta a España GC podium from last autumn. Pidcock has limited time to make the switch back to Worlds, where the punchy Montreal course would seem to suit him well. Winning a rainbow jersey on the road is perhaps Pidcock's biggest career ambition now, having won world titles in mountain bike and cyclo-cross. The 27-year-old was 10th in Rwanda last year, while his best Worlds finish came in Leuven in 2021 with sixth place.In 2027, Pidcock plans to step away from the mountain bike before a planned return in 2028 as he builds towards a shot at a third straight Olympic title.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Mads Pedersen abandons the Vuelta a España
item.content:encoded: Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) has abandoned the Vuelta a España, with the former world champion not taking to the start of Wednesday's stage 11.Despite indicating his desire to see the race through to the end, the decision has now been taken to withdraw."Unfortunately, Mads Pedersen will not take the start of today’s stage 11 of La Vuelta," read a statement from the Lidl-Trek team. "After battling illness over the past few days, Mads will now focus on making a full recovery before turning his attention to his remaining targets this season."Speaking to after stage 10, Pedersen acknowledged that the illness he'd been struggling with was "a little bit" to blame, but indicated it wasn't the full story, and that he didn't fully understand the reasons for his struggles. "I don’t really know what to say. The level is not there right now – not the shape, the shape good is good enough, but something is clearly not as it should be," he said. Pedersen, who won the road race world title in 2019, is now looking ahead to the UCI Road World Championships, with the road race taking place in Montréal on September 27. On Tuesday, Pedersen voiced his belief that fighting through to the end of the 21st and final Vuelta stage in Granada would be the best preparation for Worlds, but also heavily suggested that might not be the decision that would ultimately be made."It’s more than one guy who has to take this decision. In the end we will see. Of course I would like to keep going in the race but also it has to make sense at one point," he said on Tuesday.Pedersen placed second on stage 8 and fourth on stage 2 but was more than 10 minutes down on stage 10, which might have been a chance for victory at the height of his powers. item.title: Britain is OK with public ownership, but only by foreign powers. Why?
item.author: Maya Goodfellow
item.content:encoded: Arthur Downing, author of Power and the People: A History of British Energy, says all-encompassing rapid transition will need a mutualised systemHave you ever wondered why it is that most houses in the UK are reliant on gas boilers? Not what’s stopping more people from replacing them with heat pumps, but instead why and how the gas boiler became so ubiquitous in the first place?Arthur Downing, the author of the new book Power and the People: A History of British Energy, can tell you exactly why. “We only have boilers in our houses because of a state-owned enterprise that went into everybody’s home and installed natural gas-suitable appliances at no direct cost,” he says. The nationalised gas industry of the 1940s to the 1980s, which oversaw this huge project, was for three decades one of the “most dynamic, innovative, efficient industries in Britain”, Downing says. Yet few of us would use these terms to describe it as such now.Continue reading...

item.title: UCI Gravel World Series: Anet Barrera Esparza and Ulises Alfredo Castillo Soto win Gravel Arteaga
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: Ulises Alfredo Castillo Soto (Olinka Cycling) and Anet Barrera Esparza claimed victory at the first UCI Gravel World Series event in Mexico, Gravel Arteaga and in the process also clinched the national gravel titles, which were also decided at the event. The 133km race, started and finished in Coahuila, Arteaga, had more than 85% gravel roads and about 2,200m of elevation gain. The competition played out through high mountain stretches, with altitudes above 2,700m above sea level as well as sections through ridges and forests.Mexico's Castillo Soto won the elite men's event and national title with a time of 4:16:15, sprinting across the line just ahead of Jose Antonio Prieto De Luna, while more than 8 minutes later Angel Julian Camacho Gutierrez crossed the line to take third.Barrera claimed the Mexican title and elite women's race in emphatic style, with a time of 5:08:01 and a clear-cut solo victory. She crossed the line more than thirteen minutes ahead of second-placed Sara Roel and then it was a further eight minutes back to Venezuela's Fabiola Ariana Tucci Ron.It was one of two series events over the weekend, with Mads Würtz Schmidt and Femke Markus also claiming the European Gravel titles on Sunday. Both races, like all other series events, offered the opportunity for top finishers to qualify for the October 10 and 11 UCI Gravel World Championships, which this year is being held in Nannup, Western Australia.Elizabeth Dominguez GonzalezUlises Alfredo Castillo SotoJose Antonio Prieto De LunaAngel Julian Camacho Gutierrez Jose Miguel Reyes Morales

item.title: Kate Courtney among four elite women debuting for Team USA in the Montréal UCI Road World Championships
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: Two-time mountain bike world champion Kate Courtney continues her hit-parade season with a debut at the UCI Road World Championships for Team USA, taking place in Montréal, Canada, September 20-27.Courtney earned her spot with a victory in her first appearance at the elite women's US Pro road race championships. She then moved to an off-road campaign that included missing the defence of her Leadville Trail 100 MTB title, and signed a multi-year contract with FDJ United-SUEZ.Former US road champion Kristen Faulkner (EF Education-Oatly) returns to the lineup after missing last year's World Championships due to an injury suffered in the Tour de France Femmes. She is the only elite woman slated to ride both the time trial and the road race.Veteran Lauren Stephens (Aegis x Leaders of Enchantment)) makes her 10th appearance for Team USA and Alexis Magner (EF Education-Oatly) returns for a sixth time in her career to the Worlds. Three other elite women will compete for the first time: Grace Arlandson (Aegis x Leaders of Enchantment), Natalie Quinn (Mayenne Pro Cycling) and Taylor Knibb, a two-time US Pro time trial champion.Winning the US Pro road title for a third time, Quinn Simmons (Lidl-Trek) leads the elite men's roster that includes a total of eight riders, all of whom are part of WorldTour or ProTeam squads. EF Education-EasyPost teammates Neilson Powless and Sean Quinn join Matteo Jorgenson (Visma-Lease a Bike), Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) and Larry Warbasse (Tudor Pro) for the road race. Brandon McNulty (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) and Artem Shmidt (Netcompany Ineos) will compete in both the road race and time trial for elite men, the 22-year-old Shmidt having won the US Pro elite title in the ITT in June.The seven elite women will be joined by nine riders competing in the U23 and junior divisions for Team USA. Among that group are four riders with national titles in 2026 - U23 road race winner Katherine Sarkisov (CCB Kenetik p/b Levine Law Group), U23 time trial winner Kylee Hanel (Aegis x Leaders of Enchantment), junior women's road race winner Sophia Wellmeier (Team California Academy) and Liliana Edwards (CCB Kenetik p/b Levine Law Group).The men's roster includes 18 total riders, 10 competing in the U23 and junior divisions. The four riders who won US national titles in June are part of this group - U23 road race winner Ashlin Barry (Visma-Lease a Bike Development), U23 ITT winner Kade Kreikemeier (Meridian Racing), junior men's road race winner Enzo Hincapie (Grenke - Auto Eder) and junior men's ITT winner Kashus Adamski (Hot Tubes Cycling).Racing in downtown Montreal begins with the elite time trial races on Sunday, September 20, the women setting off at 9:00 EDT and the men at 12:45 EDT. The U23 fields competed in races against the clock on September 21, with mixed relay and junior categories competing on September 22. After an open day on Wednesday, competition resumes from September 24-27 for road races.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Ben Swift to retire from pro cycling after 18 seasons - 'I want to finish on my own terms'
item.author: laura@cyclingnews.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: Ben Swift (Netcompany Ineos) announced his plan to retire at the end of the 2026 season in a post on Instagram on Tuesday."Yeah, so this is it. I've decided to retire," Swift said. "It's been 18 great years, and never really in my wildest dreams thought I'd have such a long career and a successful career along the way. Having grown up as a kid, it was just a dream - it was always something that I never really thought would happen, but I never saw myself doing anything else, you know?"The 38-year-old began his professional cycling career in 2009 with Team Katusha, but the next year signed with Sky Procycling and remained with the organisation for all but two years, riding for UAE Team Emirates from 2017-2018.Swift came up through British Cycling's programmes, racing to his only world title on the track in the Scratch Race in 2012. Last month, he and Isle of Man teammate Matthew Bostock won the points race in the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.A sprinter with the capacity to survive smaller climbs, Swift was runner-up in Milan-San Remo in 2016 and third in 2014. While Swift scored early career wins in the Tour of California, Tour de Romandie, Tour Down Under and Tour de Pologne, and was British road race champion in 2019 and 2021, he spent most of his years as a loyal teammate, road captain and mentor for younger riders.Swift said he decided to retire on a high note. "I still love riding my bike. I love the training, I love the racing, and I think I decided to finish this year because I still feel like I'm at a high enough level to enjoy the racing," he said."There's still plenty of racing left this year. I've got Tour of Britain, which is obviously my home race. It was my first, technically, professional race. I think it was only right to go back there and do Tour of Britain. I think it'll be my 11th or 12th time riding this race, but it's just so nice to be racing in front of your home crowds on your home soil."So after Tour of Britain, I've got a few more in Italy, which is quite nice to be racing back in Italy. It feels like full circle - that's where the whole journey started. We lived in Quarrata in Tuscany in my first six years - my first three years Under-23 and then my first years pro. So I've got a real strong connection to Italy, so I think that really goes quite nicely finishing there and going full circle."And then on to Paris-Tours, so a big one to finish with. So I want to finish kind of on my own terms, on a high, enjoy my racing, and just make the most of it, you know?"For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. 'It could make his career' - Will Barta sees golden opportunity for former teammate and race leader Enric Mas in this year's Vuelta a España
item.content:encoded: 'It could make his career" is how American racer Will Barta (Tudor) views the prospects for Vuelta a España leader Enric Mas if the Spaniard takes the overall victory in his home Grand Tour.A former teammate of Mas with Movistar for four years from 2021 to 2025, 30-year-old Barta believes the overall is considerably more accessible to Mas following the abandon of Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG).As for the GC battle, Barta points to Mas' capacity to bounce back from all kinds of setbacks, such as his injury in 2025, as one of the key reasons why the Spaniard can now be fighting as hard as possible to take the overall victory."It's just nice to see him at his best - he works hard, so I'm happy for that," Barta said, referring to Mas' latest bounce back from his lengthy struggle against thrombophlebitis.Although Movistar's overall lineup in this year's Vuelta is not as strong as that of third-placed Felix Gall's Decathlon CMA CGM outfit - which will also benefit breakaways - Barta points to Movistar's lengthy Grand Tour GC heritage as a key resource when it comes to handling the pressure at the top over the next two weeks."As you saw on the Aitana [on stage 9], maybe they don't have the team to set a crazy pace, but I think they'll do it a bit more in the old school way of defending the jersey and riding conservatively."Movistar are a team that have the Grand Tour experience to do that well, even if Decathlon will likely take on their own role of setting a hard pace and isolate Enric."Barta told , is that for Movistar, leading the Vuelta for the first time since 2019, the stakes could hardly be higher."It's super exciting for them. I think the Vuelta is big for everyone, but it's an even bigger race for them."Obviously Enric is always really good in the Vuelta, and so I think it's something that they can trust in. It's the end of the season, maybe some guys are good at the beginning, and they fade a bit, but you can see Enric is always good at this time of year."Barta is currently racing his third Vuelta on the hunt for breakaways. He was feeling under the weather in the first week but is now on the up, and at a very opportune moment. Pogačar's absence undeniably changes the race, Barta argues, given UAE had a much stronger control on the race than Movistar, and that has now disappeared."With UAE they can always count on Pogačar finishing the job. Movistar have Enric, he's super good, but there are three, four or five riders that are super good too. It's not like one stands out so much from the other," he explained."So I think it's a little bit less likely that one team really takes on every stage like UAE was doing. Even on the harder mountain stages before, perhaps, it was Pogačar, Pogačar, Pogačar. Now it's more open."The question of Mas' rollercoaster career and his latest return to form makes fighting for the Vuelta even more important, Barta says, but it's also not so much of a surprise as it could seem."It shows that he's human because he has ups and downs like most riders - it's not normal to be like Pogacar, where you're always good," Barta said."I think it shows he [Mas] is human, but he's at a super level and he always fights for it. He's in great form, so this should be a good race for him""I'm sure he knows that, but he also doesn't want to put too much pressure on himself but I think it's really good for him. It could make his career."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: (Late) August P&T mailbag: Best of the worst years, all-time Knicks vs. all-time Celtics & Juju Reese
item.author: Matthew Miranda
item.content:encoded: September beckons, bitches. Let’s mailbag.What would your team look like if you assembled it from the stinky years of the 2000s-2010s?In order to tackle this question, I had to settle on what exactly “2000s-2010s” meant. We talking just the awful aughts, ending with the 2009-10 season? Or the whole stinking two decades of stank? I found myself confronted by a mystery I’d never wanted to solve: who was worse, the 2000s Knicks or the 2010s Knicks?To really get the stink marinating, I compared two nine-year abominations: the Knick teams from 2002-2010 and from 2014-2022. Combined that’s 18 seasons, 17 below .500, 16 missing the playoffs. eight losses in nine playoff games and a partridge in a pear tree. Before I give you the numbers, what does your gut tell you? Which Knicks like they were worse?From 2002-2010 the Knicks were 279-459; adjusted for 82 games that’s 31-51. The 2014-2022 Knicks went 262-450, a 30-50 pace. The numbers wouldn’t settle this debate. Futility being in the eye of the beholder, I had to dig deep. Was there anything particularly sadder about one batch versus the other? For me, there is. In 2013-14, New York was coming off a tremendous run the year before, plus three consecutive winning seasons and playoff appearances. Carmelo Anthony had just led the league in scoring while finishing third for MVP. J.R. Smith was top-20 in points, Jason Kidd top-20 in steals and Tyson Chandler top-10 in offensive rebounds, an All-Star and First Team All-Defense.The writing was on the wall once Kidd retired and James Dolan strong-armed Glenn Grunwald outta town and Andrea Bargnani in, but there was reason to feel good heading into 2014. There was excitement in 2016 for the arrival of Kristaps Porziņģis. In 2019 there was hope — if not conviction — that Kevin Durant, Kyrie Irving and Zion Williamson were on their way to save the day. The 2001-02 Knicks were post-Patrick Ewing and, not coincidentally, not good, failing to win a playoff series in 2001 for the first time since 1991. Jeff Van Gundy left, Marcus Camby and a lottery pick were soon to follow in exchange for the low point of Antonio McDyess’ career, Latrell Sprewell was almost out the door and Isiah Thomas about to walk through it. .At least the 2010s Knicks had the precedent of the 2000s teams to slightly soften the blow. Watching their initial sinking into stinking, from winning 17 playoff series in 12 years (1989-2000) to winning a single playoff game the next dozen, didn’t merely cause despair. It was a disorienting fall from grace. The 2010s were a bad headache. The 2000s were that plus vertigo.Without further ado, my ‘02-’10 Knick faves: One Saturday late in my sophomore year of college, some friends and I got in on some pickup games on campus. This was the long-gone dark ages, when I was active and thin and a pretty good baller, and that day I was . The fadeaway couldn’t miss. People were calling me Jordan. It was a very small, insignificant time and place in history, and if you weren’t literally there experiencing it in real time, it makes neither sense nor difference. So it goes with those of us who swore allegiance to the Frank Williams cult twentysomething years ago — if you weren’t there, it makes zero sense. To be fair, it didn’t make a lotta sense even if you were; Williams, a point guard, shot just 35% from the field and 30% from deep and started only three games over two years in New York. And yet if the Knicks announce tomorrow they’ve signed Williams outta retirement, I’d tell Jalen Brunson thank you for your service, now get thee to the bench. The prophecy must be fulfilled.Crawford and Lee were that restaurant that used to be open near you that was delightfully, surprisingly good. It had no business being that good, and it closed years ago. But you appreciated it when it was there, and the memories still warm you today. Looking at you, Amy’s Place in Buffalo. R.I.P.Kurt Thomas I loved because he was a true warrior for righteousness, willing to tangle with anybody and everybody who was in the wrong, no matter who it was. Whether that be a future Hall of Famer.Or the biggest fish in his own pond, like in 2004 when Thomas told Knick teammate Stephon Marbury, “Everyone in this organization is afraid of you, but I’m not. I’ll beat your ass.”Thomas joins Ewing — I think — as the only Knicks who’ve impacted winning for the club over a 14-year stretch. A key reserve for the 1999 Knicks, many of us still fondly remember the final game Thomas ever played down the stretch in 2013: the Knicks had lost a season-high four straight games and five of six as they played in Utah without Carmelo. Gutting through 27 minutes, Thomas helped the Knicks snap the losing skid and kickstart a 13-game winning streak, the finishing touch on their best season in 13 years.I hold a special place in my heart for Dr. Michael Doleac because of December 30, 2002. I was driving from Rochester to New York City and a friend tagged along looking to visit a friend in Pennsylvania. My friend considered himself hilarious for not telling me the drinks he was downing the whole drive down were spiked; by the time I figured out he was drunk, he figured out we were lost. We were “near” enough that his friend came and got him, leaving without leaving me directions to get back toward the city. It was dark out in the middle of nowhere, Pennsylvania, pre-Google maps (the less said about Mapquest, the better). I spent the drive low on gas, cursing my friend for my being lost in what looked like every horror movie ever and living and dying with the back and forth in WFAN’s broadcast of what ended up a one-point Knick win over the NBA champion Spurs. In arguably his finest hour as a ‘bocker, Doleac scored 16 points (two off his Knick-high) and grabbed eight boards (tying his Knick best) against Tim Duncan and David Robinson. I wanna end this with “This doctor makes house calls,” but the game was in New York. Then again, “This doctor takes patient visits” just doesn’t work at all. Gimme your best Doleac tag line.[List your] ranking of trades/signings/moves that built the 2026 champion Knicks.16) Drafting Pacôme Dadiet15) Signing Jeremy Sochan13) Signing Mo Diawara12) Signing Ariel Hukporti11) Drafting Miles McBride10) Signing Landry Shamet9) Drafting Mitchell Robinson 8) Trading for Mikal Bridges7) Trading for Josh Hart6) Signing Jalen Brunson’s first contract5) Trading for Karl-Anthony Towns4) Trading for OG Anunoby3) Firing Tom Thibodeau & hiring Mike Brown2) Signing Jalen Brunson’s second contract1) Hiring Leon RoseClyde and Jalen in the backcourt with Willis, Patrick and Bernard up front. From my admittedly biased perspective, this starting five could match up with any all-time mythical squad the Celtics could put together.DeanJose’s five vs. Bill Russell, Larry Bird, Kevin McHale, John Havlicek and Paul Pierce — who ya got??The Wizards traded Angel Reese’s brother Julian “Juju” Reese to the Nuggets, who then released him. While he only played 13 games (10 starts) and 30.9 minutes per game, he put up respectable numbers on a tanking team (11.8 points/10.5 rebounds, including the most offensive rebounds per game since Hakeem Olajuwon at 4.2). He’s a little undersized at 6’9, 230 lbs., but seems like a decent candidate for the third-string center job. Thoughts?First, if this is Angel Reese stanning for her , I fully understand. And email me. Please. God, please email me, Angel Reese.Assuming this is really Stan KGRY, my only thoughts are that there are definitely dudes who’ve beaten that Olajuwon number from 1987 — Dennis Rodman did a half-dozen times by himself — and that whatever downgrade there is between Mitch and Drummond, the Knicks are probably looking to make that up with an upgrade over Hukporti. You can’t count on KAT playing heavy minutes for 82 games followed by a two-month title defense, nor do I think they want to count on Drummond being the best next man up that whole time. There is 100% room for Juju Reese to make a home and career in the NBA. I don’t see it this year in New York, though.That’s all she wrote for the mailbag, and it’s gonna be all she wrote for a while. I’m now writing about the Knicks at OnSI, and no longer at P&T. I’ve left before and returned; this feels less like “Goodbye” than “Later.” I’ll still pop into the comments sometimes, and have a few other pots starting to boil. Email if you want. I’m on Bluesky. I love you all. Not all. But you, reading this now, I love. Yes, you.

item.title: 'We're sending Tadej healing vibes' - UAE Team Emirates-XRG teammates at Vuelta a España fighting for injured Pogačar from afar
item.content:encoded: When Pavel Sivakov stood on the Vuelta a España sign-on podium on Tuesday to receive his award for the previous stage's most combative rider, it was a timely reminder of how UAE Team Emirates-XRG now have no choice following Tadej Pogačar's abandon but to switch objectives completely from the GC to stage wins.Once again, Sivakov and Kevin Vermaercke, both in the breakaways on stage 9, were extremely active in the late moves that materialized on stage 10, too, as riders tested Cofidis and Visma-Lease a Bike's willingness to try and keep things under control for a bunch sprint.As UAE riders told media pre-stage in the mixed zone, despite his enforced absence, Pogačar remained very much uppermost in their thoughts, with the team following his recovery progress from afar. And, the Slovenian was reportedly keeping an eye on their progress in the race, too."Morale obviously could be better, but we're continuing on and sending Tadej healing vibes," teammate Jay Vine told at the stage start."At this point, trying to get back is probably not on the forefront of his mind, but trying just to recover and reset for the next goals."Our objective is breakaway stages. We'll see how everyone's going on these next stages but it [Tuesday] is also a good opportunity for [Visma] to control the race for their two fast guys as well."The operation to repair a fractured clavical on Monday afternoon and early evening was carried out by the well-known Catalan orthopedic surgeon Xavier Mir, newspaper reported. Dr. Mir is famous for having treated a large number of MotoGP pilots for various injuries."We know he's had the operation [on his collarbone] and that it's gone well," teammate Ivo Oliveira told , "and we're hoping he recovers as quickly as possible."He's still watching the Vuelta, he's fan of the team and of the race, we've got a great group here even without Tadej and Pablo [Torres, who abandoned on stage 9 - Ed.]."Saturday was complicated because we went [from' having for one leader to a team fighting for breaks. But [Sports Director Joxean] Matxin talked to us, and he told us we still had things to fight for in the Vuelta, but we'd have to change mentality. And that's what we've done."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Nepal-Tibet flood deaths pass 1,000 as police ask relatives for DNA to identify victims
item.author: Cait Kelly in Kathmandu and agencies
item.content:encoded: Relatives of missing tourists asked for blood samples and photos, as efforts continue to rescue trapped hydropower workersNepali rescuers have built temporary bridges to reach remote areas and dug through the ruins of hydropower projects in the Himalayas to rescue hundreds of trapped workers, as the death toll passed 1,000 nearly ⁠a week after devastating ​floods left a trail of destruction across the country’s towns and valleys.About 600 people remain stuck in several devastated hydropower stations that have become the focus of rescue efforts. The prime ⁠minister, Balendra Shah, said more than 11,000 people had been rescued across the affected region, and power and communication lines had been restored in some areas.Continue reading...

item.title: 'Initially frustrated, but mostly disappointed' - Switch of tactics at Vuelta a España fails to reward Wout van Aert and Visma-Lease a Bike
item.content:encoded: An unexpected switch of roles by Visma-Lease a Bike at the Vuelta a España on stage 10 certainly kept their rivals guessing, but finally failed to pay off as Wout van Aert finished fourth after his teammates Matthew Brennan and Sepp Kuss kept the breakaways under control.Brennan and Van Aert had pulled off a stunning two-part strategy on stage 2, with the Belgian attacking in the closing kilometres, drawing out the peloton and even keeping then-race leader Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) in check before the Briton then sprinted for the win.After Van Aert and Christophe Laporte had then provided Brennan with a stunning leadout on stage 4, six days later on the category 3 climb of Puerto de Socovos, Brennan was a constant presence in the stream of attacks that materialised and helped to clamp them down.Finally, on the grinding uphill to Elche de la Sierra, Sepp Kuss jumped out of the pack on a couple of occasions, in an echo of the role he played in Van Aert's victory in Cordoba two years ago, burying himself on the front of the pack to ensure it stayed together in the closing kilometres.Still, he told assembled media, in comments reported by later, the teamwork could not be faulted, and he was sure that his first stage win in the 2026 Vuelta and fourth of his career was just around the corner, too."Matthew is a great guy and we have helped each other many times already. The whole team threw themselves into it, and if we keep going like this, we will come out on top again, I am sure of that," Van Aert said."I was initially frustrated, but mostly disappointed. You want to finish it off, and in the sprint, I didn't have enough left in my legs."The last 30 kilometers were chaotic, and I really needed all my teammates to make it come down to a sprint. I am incredibly grateful for this opportunity. If we keep going like this, we will continue to be successful."Van Aert said that he could have made some errors of positioning in the lengthy uphill battle in Elche de la Sierra, but he would first need to check the video to see what happened. "In any case," he recognised, "when it came to the last key corner with 650 metres to go, I wasn't close enough to the front."That meant he had to expend a lot of energy just to get back up to the front and that made his own options very limited. As he put it simply afterwards, "I'm pretty bummed about that".Van Aert made a point of repeatedly thanking his teammates, particularly on a day that, as he said, the collaboration for a sprint had been very limited. Only Cofidis, pushing hard for another victory with Bryan Coquard, were willing to give a hand.Asked by if he felt guilty at having had Brennan work for him but failing to get the win afterwards, Van Aert answered frankly, "Of course, that’s what puts pressure on both of us. He feels same pressure when I'm doing a leadout for him."But we know how to handle this very well. There have been a lot of doubts and questions, from outside our team about this whole Vuelta. But we have the green jersey, we've won two stages. If we continue the spirit in the team where you give and you take, then there are no issues."Wednesday's stage into Lorca will likely end in another bunch sprint battle, although given the terrain is much flatter throughout - 1,300 metres of vertical climbing compared to the nearly 3,000 tackled by the peloton on Tuesday - it remains to be seen what strategy Visma will take. Either way, and whether the Dutch squad opt for Brennan's third stage of the 2026 race or Van Aert's first, both the Belgian and the Briton will be keen to be back in the thick of the action once again.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Pogačar's crash doesn't just put his Worlds defence in doubt, it complicates next season's plans – Sean Kelly's Vuelta column
item.content:encoded: We won't know for certain until the UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider is out of hospital and we get a clearer picture of his condition, but from what people are saying and what I've been looking at, it could be several weeks.It might therefore be too difficult for him to get back into shape for his end-of-season goals, notably the World Championships in Montréal, the Europeans on his home roads of Slovenia, and a tilt at a record-breaking sixth Il Lombardia. Saturday could well have been the end of his season.I suspect there'll be a lot of his fellow riders with a keen interest in the outcome of Pogačar's operation, thinking to themselves, 'I have a much better chance of winning a rainbow jersey now.'Perhaps more disappointing for Pogačar than potentially missing out on the chance to make it three world championship titles in a row, or break the record in Lombardy, is the fact that La Vuelta's red jersey still eludes him. He was going to tick it off this year, and then that would be done, but now he's going to have to think about when he will return to the Spanish Grand Tour, because that's the type of champion he is; he doesn't want any races missing from his palmarès. It certainly complicates matters further for next season.Not bad bike handling, just bad luckLooking at the crash more closely, it appears to have been just one loose stone, and he had no idea what was on the road ahead. I suspect his hands slipped off the handlebars because of the way he went over the bike and banged off the Visma-Lease a Bike riders – it's just a bit of bad luck, unfortunately. And in fairness to Pogačar, one of his many great attributes is his bike handling. You can only really count a handful of occasions where he's come unstuck. And he's only suffered serious fractures on this occasion and at the 2023 Liège-Bastogne-Liège, when he fractured his wrist in a similar incident. While those are both unlucky, his avoidance of crashes isn't down to luck; it's because he's a naturally strong bike handler. Going downhill in the bunch, in windy conditions or in echelons on the flat stages, we've seen it so many times, and that's what makes him so difficult to challenge in these Grand Tours. I've said that many times before; there's no weak point.Even on those occasions where he's had dicey moments, like at Paris-Roubaix or Strade Bianche last year when he went too hot into a corner, he managed to get away unscathed. While Milan-San Remo this year was purely a crash I put down to bike racing – it's nothing to do with bike handling. So Saturday's incident is something he'll probably be sat in hospital thinking about, and cursing, because there was nothing he could do. One silver lining is that this incident came at this point in the season, rather than at or in the build-up to the Tour de France. For a rider targeting a spot in the general classification at this race, maybe a top-three or top-five, it wouldn't be the end of the world to bow out early. But when you're in a position like Pogačar's, in the maillot rojo and riding towards Granada at a canter, with a really favourable World Championships course on the horizon too, it's going to be a disappointment. It could be a whole lot worse, though.Six or seven riders could still win La VueltaReflecting on the now Pogačar-less La Vuelta, when you look at Sunday's stage, in particular the final mountain, the racing was great. It was on all the way until the final two kilometres, with plenty of suspense. Who will win the stage? Who will gain time on who? Who could lose time? I hate to say it, but if we had Pogačar there, he'd probably have ridden away from the rest of the bunch and arrived 40 seconds ahead of his closest rival, essentially killing off any suspense with four or five kilometres, maybe even more, still to race.So the stage had a lot more suspense in the final. Of course, you can't deny or lament what Pogačar does on these occasions; it's amazing stuff. But the racing isn't typically as exciting as it was on Sunday, or as it will be throughout the mountaintop finishes coming up this week.Which rider comes to the fore over the days to come and fills that Pogačar-shaped hole remains to be seen. You could make an argument for each of the top six or seven riders in the GC for why they could win La Vuelta. The current leader, Enric Mas, looks to be riding the wave of the red jersey, and he's been impressive. I've always marked the Movistar man as a 'follower', following moves but rarely ever attacking himself, so I wondered how he would ride now, with the leader's jersey on his back and all eyes on him, but he did so magnificently.However, there's no shortage of riders to knock Mas off his perch. Richard Carapaz is one man who has come into this race carrying good form from the Tour de France and is a dangerous fox in the high mountains, but will fatigue catch up with him come the final week?If four-time winner Primož Roglič stays where he is in the standings for the individual time trial, then he's going to be dangerous too. The Slovenian had ridden fewer than 30 racedays before La Vuelta, and I've heard grumblings that he's not proving great value for Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe's money, but another Grand Tour title will surely change all that.Oscar Onley, like Roglič, has also had his injury issues this campaign, and the Netcompany-Ineos rider has shifted his focus to a La Vuelta GC bid as a result. He's clearly got some good form to be up there on Sunday, and perhaps will only get stronger as the race goes on. It's crazy to think we've still got two more full weeks of racing to come, considering the drama that La Vuelta has already delivered. With several serious mountain days in both weeks, it's going to be a difficult and tactically interesting battle, that's for certain.

item.title: Gillies, Child and five-star Grant top Oulton Park Gold Cup
Haas rules out switch to 2027 development as VF-26 updates coming in Monza
The mysterious erasure of RJ Barrett
item.author: Russell Richardson
item.content:encoded: Really, how often do you remember Rowan Junior?Mayor Zohran Mamdani did. Speaking at the Knicks’ championship ceremony at City Hall on June 18, he made sure RJ Barrett’s name was included among those who helped build the title team:“This championship belongs to them too, because championships aren’t just built in one season. It belongs to Immanuel Quickley, RJ Barrett, Donte DiVincenzo, Julius Randle, and also to a coach who also laid the groundwork, Tom Thibodeau.”Still, Barrett has become strangely easy to overlook when we talk about the era that began with Thibodeau, Julius Randle, and the 2020–21 “We Here” Knicks. On this date, September 1, 2022, RJ signed an extension that appeared to establish him as part of the long-term core; 16 months later, he became the central piece of the trade that brought OG Anunoby to New York.Rowan Alexander “RJ” Barrett Jr. arrived with bona fide basketball bloodlines. His father, Rowan Barrett Sr., starred at St. John’s, played professionally overseas, captained Canada at the 2000 Olympics, and later became general manager of Canada Basketball. His mother, Kesha, was a nationally ranked sprinter and long jumper at St. John’s. Steve Nash, one of the greatest Canadian basketball players ever, is RJ’s godfather. With all that preceding him, clearly young RJ was destined to be a professional bowler.Born in Toronto in 2000, Barrett starred at St. Marcellinus before transferring to Montverde Academy in Florida. By the end of his high school career, he was the consensus No. 1 recruit in the class of 2018, with Naismith Prep Player of the Year and Gatorade National Player of the Year honors in his trophy case.Barrett entered Duke as the projected top pick in the 2019 draft, but his roommate Zion Williamson quickly became the main attraction in Durham. The two became close friends, referred to each other as brothers, and made history as the first freshman teammates to each average more than 20 points. Williamson’s gravitational pull (literal and figurative) pushed Barrett into the background somewhat, even as RJ set ACC freshman scoring records and earned consensus first-team All-American honors.Meanwhile, the 2018–19 Knicks were deliberately dreadful, finishing 17–65 during the first season of the new lottery odds. Their 14% chance at Williamson turned into the third pick, with New Orleans selecting Zion and Memphis taking Ja Morant. Barrett was still considered a top-three talent and a clean fit for New York, so the Knicks pounced without hesitation. Still…he wasn’t Zion. (I still think about the woman who got the Zion Knicks tattoo ahead of draft night and wonder if she still has it…)On draft night at Barclays Center, RJ became emotional when Adam Silver called his name, later explaining that his late maternal grandfather, a die-hard Knicks fan with Brooklyn and Jamaica roots, used to tell him he would someday play for the club. After his press conference, Barrett turned toward the cameras and declared, “Yo! I’m a Knick!” His excitement was so sweetly genuine: he wanted New York, and New York wanted him right back (but…he still wasn’t Zion…).Barrett’s rookie season was uneven, with 14.3 points per game on inefficient shooting. Thibodeau’s arrival changed the direction of the franchise and helped Barrett find firmer footing. He averaged 17.6 points in 2020–21, improved his shooting, defended harder, and helped Randle carry New York into the playoffs for the first time since 2013.RJ reached 20 points per game the following season and continued to start nearly every night. When the Knicks extended him in September 2022, Barrett was only 22 and still looked like a key piece in whatever New York was becoming.The fit never completely worked, though. Barrett and Randle both did their best work inside the arc, which cramped the paint, and Barrett never became a reliable enough three-point shooter or natural enough playmaker to solve the problem (particularly after Captain Brunson arrived). He could still bully his way downhill and occasionally produce a great Garden moment. His banked-in buzzer-beater that completed a comeback against Boston in January 2022 is a recent classic. Consistency, however, remained elusive.Then, on December 30, 2023, the Knicks sent Barrett, Immanuel Quickley, and a second-round pick to Toronto for Anunoby, Precious Achiuwa, and Malachi (Evil Donte) Flynn. Anunoby’s defense and seamless fit transformed the team almost immediately, and it quickly became a pretty lopsided trade.For Barrett, the deal meant going home. He became a steady 20-point scorer in Toronto, showed growth as a playmaker, and continued using his strength to batter his way toward the rim. Life hit him with tragedy when his younger brother Nathan died following an illness in March 2024. Barrett stepped away from basketball before eventually returning and speaking openly about his grief: “He was my best friend…I’m always missing him. I still text him.” Our hearts went out to him and still do.The championship story understandably centers on Brunson, Anunoby, Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, and Josh Hart. We love them all, but none were on the team when RJ arrived. MSG was still a sort of basketball wasteland. RJ brought some hope that someday soon, things would be different. He absorbed the expectations that came with being the third pick on a miserable team, helped the Knicks climb out of the lottery years, and supplied his share of memorable nights at the Garden. Mamdani remembered, and a few others still do. For a player once expected to become the face of the franchise, his name should come up more often.

item.title: ‘I feel like I’m grieving’: staff on the devastating fallout of widespread layoffs at Xbox
item.author: Keith Stuart
item.content:encoded: Last month, Microsoft’s gaming division told its workforce it was cutting 3,200 jobs, which some say will have big ramifications for game development – as well as taking a huge personal tollOn the morning of 6 July, an email went out from Asha Sharma, the chief executive of Xbox, to all of the division’s employees around the world. Under the headline “Resetting Xbox”, it announced the most significant restructuring in the history of Microsoft’s console business: 3,200 staff would be laid off throughout the financial year to 2027, and 1,600 of those roles would be eliminated immediately.An hour later, at studios throughout company, the Teams meeting invites started arriving. “It was a virtual call with our studio manager,” says Anne Barrett, who was laid off from Bethesda Game Studios Austin. “All of our cameras and microphones were turned off so we weren’t able to say anything or react to anything. We were just brought in, told the news and it was like: ‘You guys are going to lose access to your Slack channel.’ So you saw a flurry of goodbye messages before everything was just shut off.”Continue reading...

item.title: Knicks Domino Effects: What if Jalen Brunson stayed in Dallas?
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: Domino effects are meant to start relatively small. The first two editions of the series, I feel like, encompassed that. We got really niche with the Mike Brown Kings saga and less niche with Julius Randle’s injury, but both of them required a lot of outside-the-box thinking to see directly what a reversal would’ve caused to the Knicks’ long-term hopes.This one is anything but niche.To wrap up this mini-series I’ve had fun with over the dog days of the summer, we’re going to look at possibly the biggest domino effect of them all, one that was scarily realistic and only didn’t occur because of the hubris of a certain front office that later made one of the worst trades in NBA history.You saw the title. This is a scenario that Jalen Brunson, the birthday boy and the man who has exceeded every expectation and has spearheaded a revival of Knicks basketball so grand that all of us have spent way too much money on championship merch, never puts on the orange and blue.Following his third season in Dallas, Brunson and his agents at CAA wanted to negotiate a contract extension with the Mavericks’ brass. The number that they decided on was more than reasonable for a player of his current production: four years and $55 million. After all, he was coming off finishing fourth in Sixth Man of the Year voting with plausible upward mobility. Dallas said no. Fast forward a few months: as Brunson began what turned out to be a breakout campaign, he and his agent approached the Mavs again about the same framework and were again told no. Brunson kept working and gradually improving to the point where the Mavs themselves approached him about the $55 million deal after the trade deadline, but at that point, he had outgrown that offer as he was barreling towards free agency. Four months later, he landed in New York on a four-year, $104 million pact.But what if Dallas realized what they had in Brunson at either one of those points, particularly the in-season extension? What if they took a guy that the Knicks had long been looking at off the market? Such a deal would’ve been more than reasonable for their current cap structure as a sixth man or starter next to Luka Doncic, even if the fit was potentially difficult due to both of their defensive shortcomings. Frankly, it was nonsensical for them to be that blind. This was a good player.December 1, 2021. Jalen Brunson and the Dallas Mavericks announce a four-year, $55 million extension that will begin the following season. Let’s see where the dominoes fall.Nothing changes from this point forward on any side for the rest of the 2021-22 season. Brunson still balls out and gets on the national radar with his incredible performance in the postseason; the Knicks still miss the playoffs, etc. Instead of the media clowning the Knicks for giving Brunson a nine-figure deal in June, the offseason is spent lauding Nico Harrison and company for their wherewithal to lock down this impact player for cheap.Of course, this creates a gigantic path of divergence for the Knicks, who were always infatuated with Brunson because of his family connections. I still think Rick Brunson gets hired onto Tom Thibodeau’s staff to replace the outgoing Kenny Payne (who had a truly disastrous tenure at Louisville). The hiring was definitely motivated by his son’s free agency, but he had also served as an assistant under Thibs in Chicago and Minnesota, so it still happens.The real question, though, is what happens in that offseason. Our first major question revolves around the strategy for the 2022 NBA Draft, particularly with the No. 11 overall pick.For those who don’t remember, the Knicks selected Ousmane Dieng, traded him to the Thunder in exchange for three first-round picks, traded up to No. 13 in exchange for two picks, selected Jalen Duren, and shipped him to Detroit alongside Kemba Walker in an effective salary dump. The team came out with solid assets and cleared up some cash.The motivation behind punting a lottery pick? Signing Jalen Brunson. A later trade with Detroit shipped Alec Burks and Nerlens Noel to the Motor City and cleared up just enough space for the Villanova alum and Isaiah Hartenstein in free agency. It’s why I never cared about people saying “the Knicks traded Jalen Duren for nothing” because it’s false. You don’t get Brunson (most likely) without trading Duren, his cap hit, and the salary attached. But with Brunson off the table and no clear reason to use cap space, the Knicks are dead set on picking in the lottery. You might think it’s as simple as drafting Dieng or Duren, but the Knicks almost certainly made both selections on behalf of the teams they were actively negotiating with. After all, if they wanted them, they wouldn’t trade them.There were a few plans for this draft leading up to it. After the Knicks were once again denied a chance at lottery luck, they constantly rang the phones to try to trade up for Jaden Ivey. They may get over the line for this. After all, with no Brunson on the way, there are no schematic issues.It would still be a very difficult trade to make, so I lean toward it not happening. After Ivey, they seemed quite enamored with Wisconsin guard Johnny Davis, but the Wizards took him 10th overall. That’s two major bullets dodged, but who’s on the clock at No. 11?The available players who had a pre-draft workout in New York were AJ Griffin, Tari Eason, MarJon Beauchamp, and Mark Williams. I would think it would be one of these guys, even if the extremely talented Jalen Williams and Duren were on the board. In typical Leon Rose fashion, he probably does the first two trades of the night, where he trades out and comes back in, ultimately scooping up two conditional firsts from Detroit and Washington while trading four seconds. With the 13th pick, they select Duke wing AJ Griffin.With no Brunson and an unsuccessful pursuit of both Davis and Ivey in the draft, the Knicks badly need a point guard. I’d assume they still look to offload salary, particularly with Kemba, to open cap space, but the extent of this is unclear due to the lack of a clear alternative in free agency. There’s restricted free agent Collin Sexton, of course, but the direction that needs to be taken appears to be in the trade market. Fortunately, there are two lead guards available.Dejounte Murray is on the block in San Antonio and could be had for a reasonable package. His defensive fortitude makes him a welcome fit for a team that has major defensive questions, and his offense has also proven capable of a leap forward. There’s also that New York native out in Utah who could be of use…For Murray, the Knicks never seemed that motivated to make that move, even if he would’ve been a decent fit next to Brunson in real life. They were always more focused on adding Donovan Mitchell and figuring it out later. In this timeline, Murray still goes to Atlanta, but it’s a full-court press on bringing Spida home.With no Brunson, there’s nothing holding them back from adding a small guard into the fray. The fit concerns aren’t there. When Danny Ainge and the Jazz ask for a ridiculous package, it’s eventually negotiated down into something the team can agree on. In mid-August 2022, Mitchell comes home for a package centered around RJ Barrett and Quentin Grimes, depleting the team’s draft capital to keep further players out of the deal. As much as fans want to play the kids, the Knicks see an opportunity to compete and take it.Thus, here’s the rotation we have heading into the 2022-23 season:Donovan Mitchell – Derrick RoseEvan Fournier – Immanuel QuickleyAlec Burks – Cam Reddish/AJ GriffinJulius Randle – Obi ToppinMitchell Robinson – Isaiah HartensteinYes, in this reality, we assume that the Knicks still find a way to get off Noel’s contract but keep Burks as wing depth after trading Barrett and Grimes. Hartenstein was always a target for the front office and still comes to New York.This lineup, as you might imagine, would’ve been rather erratic. You have some brilliant shotmakers in there, but not enough defenders. Tom Thibodeau’s seat gets hot again; he’s forced to bench some players permanently, and the mini-revival still happens… to an extent.Quickley gets a chance to start with Spida, Deuce McBride’s emergence happens a year sooner, Randle enjoys his bounce-back season. The foundation of the start of the Brunson era would’ve likely been similar, but the real repercussions come later.At the deadline, the team needs wing depth, having iced Reddish out of the rotation. With Brunson no longer on the team, I can’t imagine the interest in Josh Hart is any more pronounced. It’s still possible that the trade happens. I’m instead going to involve the Knicks in the multi-team trade with the Warriors and Pistons that got Gary Payton II back to the Bay. The Knicks send a bucket of seconds and Cam Reddish to Detroit for Saddiq Bey.With Mitchell, the Knicks win 48 games and slide into the fourth seed in the Eastern Conference, where they host a Cavs team that never got the New York native and instead had to continue building around Darius Garland, Sexton, and Evan Mobley. The Knicks still win in five.In the second round, the Bucks still get slayed by the wrath of Jimmy Butler and the Heat, and although many fans are optimistic about the prospects of facing the No. 8 seed, Butler waxes the Knicks in a six-game defeat.Heading into the following season, the Knicks are content with what they got, planning to use it as a building year. Burks never being traded means there’s not enough space to sign Donte DiVincenzo, who was also likely going to be someone Brunson pitched signing. There’s no big move to be made here, so we keep going into a shaky start to the 2023-24 season, which leaves them at an inflection point around the New Year.As you might recall, OG Anunoby was acquired in real life on December 30, 2023, for RJ Barrett, Immanuel Quickley, and a second-round pick. In this reality, Barrett is already gone, but Quickley is becoming a foundational piece after being started out of necessity midway through the prior season. The financials still work if the Knicks add Burks to the trade, but with Barrett not included, the rest of the team’s excess draft capital goes with it.The Big 3 of Spida-Anunoby-Randle destroy the competition in January 2024 until injuries take out both Randle and Anunoby. Mitchell does his best to imitate 2024 Brunson and gets First-Team All-NBA for his troubles, but it’s certainly an uphill climb. Without DiVincenzo to help with off-ball scoring, the Knicks only win 46 games, dropping them to the play-in tournament. Remember, the No. 2 and No. 7 seeds were just three games apart that year.The Knicks get revenge on the Heat in the 7-8 game, but have to fare with a road series against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Bucks in the first round, one that just doesn’t go well. With no Randle to physically match up, Toppin (who I believe doesn’t get traded with the team’s worst depth the prior season) and Precious Achiuwa are overwhelmed in a six-game defeat. The front office blames injuries and doesn’t make any drastic moves… yet.The Mikal Bridges trade never happens. They had to use a boatload of draft assets to get Anunoby and Mitchell, so the Nets aren’t interested. Anunoby extends, Spida gets his three-year, $150 million extension, and the Knicks seem prepared to run it back in 2024-25.Now, you might wonder: what about KAT?The Knicks badly wanted him, but they lacked a guy who Minnesota really valued in DiVincenzo to get it done. Further, the fact that Mitchell took a max extension puts the team eerily close to the second apron, something they avoided with Brunson’s pay cut. There’s a very realistic world that this trade doesn’t happen, but Leon Rose always gets his guy, so they trade Mitchell Robinson and the last bits of draft capital to get it done.It’s not worth prognosticating who fills the Hart and Bridges gaps in the lineup, but the Knicks are built around Mitchell, Anunoby, and Towns. That Big 3 would get two seasons to work everything out, going into the second apron in 2025-26 before James Dolan would order a restructuring. They had to win. They had no choice. In the first year, they get bounced in the second round by the Celtics after a 52-win season. The poise of the Brunson-led Knicks was a big part of why they came back from all those deficits, plus the team would be utterly devoid of defensive length without Robinson or Bridges. This also means that the Knicks and Pacers never rekindle their rivalry in either season, which is fun to think about.In 2025-26, the year we all rejoiced in real life, they had a real chance. They fortified the depth; they hired Mike Brown to replace Thibs; they waltzed into an extremely weak East and grabbed the bull by the horns.50 wins in the regular season, enough for the No. 3 seed. They survived a seven-game war with Atlanta, took out Philadelphia in six games, and went face-to-face with the Pistons in the ECF. Remember, no Mitchell likely dooms the Cavs to mediocrity and no ECF berth. It’s hard to say for sure if the Pistons give the Knicks the same fits they did in real life, but let’s look at the facts. The Knicks were still a major question mark defensively and had no answer for Cade Cunningham. Additionally, they lacked the presence of Robinson (even in a backup role) to fluster Duren. In a tense, seven-game series, the Pistons prevailed. It’s over.Mitchell would not be extended again by the Knicks, as his playoff shortcomings would not be worth the $270 million extension he got in real life. I’d think the front office would side with the Big Bodega in this, and the team would be built around the fleeting prime of Towns from here.Safe to say, no banners. Sad stuff. But how’s Jalen doing in Dallas?Brunson’s New Life In DallasDallas did basically nothing that offseason to replace Brunson, leaving them inherently weaker entering the 2022-23 season. They still acquire Christian Wood after retaining Brunson, but they feel pretty stagnant.The big change in the 2022-23 season is that the Mavericks never traded for Kyrie Irving, as the fit with him, Brunson, and Luka would’ve been quite bizarre. They also wouldn’t feel the need to, as when Doncic goes down with injury right before the deadline, we see glimpses of Knicks Brunson in the emerging Villanova alum.Dallas was quite bad this season, flaming out in the play-in tournament, but an interesting trickle-down effect from this is that they wouldn’t be able to properly tank to keep their draft pick, so a parting gift from Brunson would give the Knicks a lottery pick in 2023, which they’d use on a guy like Jordan Hawkins. Not a needle mover, so I didn’t feel the need to mention until now.The reverb would be no Dereck Lively II in Dallas, but the supporting cast from guys like PJ Washington and eventually Daniel Gafford would provide enough for the Mavericks to still go deep in the postseason in 2024, maybe making the NBA Finals but still not coming that close to a title.At the same time that all appears to be well in Dallas, Nico Harrison is stirring. He doesn’t like the frequent unavailability of Doncic, who still suffers a major hamstring injury on Christmas 2024. In his absence, unlike in real life where Kyrie suffered a multi-week injury as well, the Mavericks experience the joy of 2024 Jalen Brunson, who carries Dallas through January to the point where Harrison has an epiphany.“What if I fortify my defense and Jalen can give me Luka-esque production?”Brunson’s explosion dooms Doncic’s tenure, as the controversial trade with the Lakers still occurs. Anthony Davis would now be paired with a head of the snake in Brunson, a match seemingly made in heaven.Except Davis is still injury-prone. Dallas never has the death spiral they had with Davis and Irving’s season-ending injuries because Brunson would be there trying to play hero ball. He does just enough to win them 45 games to take the No. 9 seed. After defeating Sacramento in the 9-10 game, a heroic 40-ball sees them stun the Grizzlies to steal a playoff spot, only to get eviscerated by the powerhouse Thunder.This turns out to be an utter disaster, as Cooper Flagg will no longer become a Maverick. It was possible to have a core of Brunson, Davis, and Flagg, but now? Brunson hits his 30th birthday with Davis shipped to Washington and a band of merrymen around him.That’s right. The real twist of all of this? Nobody wins.The Knicks lose because they don’t have Brunson. They never sniff the NBA Finals.The Mavericks lose because the domino effect takes two lottery picks away, and JB’s hyper-competitiveness doesn’t allow them to get younger.Jalen Brunson loses. Instead of being the King of New York, he’s got a microscope on him in lowly Dallas as the guy Nico traded Luka to feature.It’s a lose-lose situation. What a nightmare. I need my nightlight; someone turn on some highlights.That’s better. Happy Birthday, Cap. We’re so glad this never happened.
